## Setup

### Load shared settings, packages, themes and colour palettes

`common.R` sets the global `knitr` chunk options (warnings/messages off, figures
centred), loads every package used in this report (tidyverse, ComplexHeatmap,
ggtree, DT, plotly, ...) and defines the reusable ggplot themes
(`sofonias_theme`), colour palettes and helper functions (`create_dt`, `%!in%`)
that are referenced throughout the document.

```{r}
source("common.R")
```

## Extracting the K13 flanking region from the VCF

### Subset the joint VCF to Gondar samples and to the 200 kb window around *k13*

These commands were run once on the command line (kept here with `eval=FALSE`
for provenance only). In order they:

1. `bcftools view -S gondar.txt` - keep only the Gondar samples from the filtered,
   bi-allelic, VQSLOD-filtered joint SNP call set.
2. `bcftools index` - index the resulting compressed VCF.
3. `bcftools view -r Pf3D7_13_v3:1625133-1825133` - cut out a 200 kb window
   centred on the *k13* locus on chromosome 13.
4. `vcf2matrix.py` - convert that regional VCF into a binary genotype matrix
   (`0` = reference, `1` = alternate, `NA` = missing) which is what all the
   downstream haplotype clustering uses.

```{bash,eval=FALSE}
# bcftools view -S /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/flanking_haplotype_updated/gondar.txt  /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/ethiopia_vcf/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps_ethiopia.vcf.gz -Oz -o /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/ethiopia_vcf/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps_ethiopia_gonder.vcf.gz

# bcftools index /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/ethiopia_vcf/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps_ethiopia_gonder.vcf.gz

# bcftools view -r Pf3D7_13_v3:1625133-1825133 /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/ethiopia_vcf/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps_ethiopia_gonder.vcf.gz -Oz -o /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/ethiopia_vcf/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps_ethiopia_gonder_flanking_k13.vcf.gz

# conda activate fastq2matrix

# python ~/software/fastq2matrix/scripts/vcf2matrix.py --vcf /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/ethiopia_vcf/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps_ethiopia_gonder_flanking_k13.vcf.gz --no-iupacgt --na NA --threads 4 

```

### Build the sample sets and slice the genome-wide binary matrix

Rather than starting from scratch, the genome-wide binary matrix is subset
directly. One major factor that affects a flanking-haplotype picture is sample
clonality, so the sample lists are built so that the all-sample result can later
be compared with a monoclonal-only result (previously all samples were used).

This chunk:

* reads the genome-wide binary matrix (`*.mat.bin`) and drops the `chr`/`ref`
  columns, leaving `pos` plus one column per sample;
* reads the per-site $F_{WS}$ table and defines **monoclonal** samples as
  $F_{WS} \ge 0.94$ (a slightly relaxed threshold because of small differences
  between the locally computed and the published $F_{WS}$ values);
* reads the *k13* genotype table and keeps only samples carrying the **622I**
  variant (`genotype` containing a `1`);
* builds two sample sets - Gondar + Eritrean 622I carriers, and
  Gambella + Uganda + South-East Asia samples for the **675V** comparison;
* slices the matrix to a 50 kb window around 622I (1,705,133-1,755,133; target
  position 1,725,133) and a 40 kb window around 675V (1,704,974-1,744,974;
  target position 1,724,974).

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)
library(dendextend)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)
all_mat_bin <- read.table(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/012026_pf_mgen_ug_india_eritrea_ethiopia_popgen.filt.csq.bi.GT.miss0.2.vqslod.filt.snps.mat.bin",
  header = T
) %>%
  select(-c(chr, ref))
samples <- data.frame(sample = colnames(all_mat_bin)[-(1:0)])
fws_site <- read.table(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/fws/fws_by_site.tsv",
  header = T
)
monoclonal <- fws_site %>%
  filter(fws >= 0.94) # i use this threshold since there are some differerences in calculation of fws with the one i generated and leen
suppleme_fws <- read.csv(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/supplementary_Data/supp_fws_up.tsv",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  select(sample_id, Country, fws)


# this is to extract samples which contain the k13 622I varaint
k13_622I <- read.csv(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/genotype_extraction/k13_target/target_positions_genotypes_k13.csv",
  header = T
) %>%
  filter(grepl("1", genotype))
# gambella , uganda and south east asia samples to do the flanking haplotype analysis around the 675 variant
gambella_ug_se_675_samples <- read.table(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/flanking_haplotype_updated/gambella_675/gambella_ug_SE.txt",
  header = T
)

gondar_eritrea_sample <- read.table(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/flanking_haplotype_updated/k13_gondar_eritrea/gondar_eritrea.txt",
  header = T
)

eritrian_622I <- k13_622I %>%
  filter(grepl("ERR", sample)) %>%
  select(sample) %>%
  dplyr:::rename(wgs_id = sample)

gondar_sample_er_622I <- gondar_eritrea_sample %>% # run the first for gondar and eritria
  filter(grepl("GM", wgs_id)) %>%
  full_join(eritrian_622I)

# this is to make sure that the samples are monoclonal

# for extracting samples and positions from the binary matrix file
df_filtered <- all_mat_bin[,
  colnames(all_mat_bin) %in% c("pos", gondar_sample_er_622I$wgs_id)
]
filtered_data <- df_filtered[
  df_filtered$pos >= 1705133 & df_filtered$pos <= 1755133,
] # change this positions for start and end , the range size is 20000bp

df_filtered_675 <- all_mat_bin[,
  colnames(all_mat_bin) %in% c("pos", gambella_ug_se_675_samples$sample)
]
# 675  position is 1724974
filtered_data_675 <- df_filtered_675[
  df_filtered_675$pos >= 1704974 & df_filtered_675$pos <= 1744974,
] # change this positions for start and end
```

### `make_flanking_heatmap()` - draw the SNP heatmap around a target variant

Several parameters change the appearance of a flanking-haplotype plot: the size
of the window, which samples are included, and the distance metric used for
clustering (Euclidean here, with Ward.D2 linkage). Widening the window increases
the chance of picking up unrelated variants, which can change the clustering, so
the window and the metric are passed in explicitly and reported in the plot
title.

The function:

* transposes the position-by-sample matrix into samples-by-position, replaces
  missing calls with `0` and recodes heterozygous `0.5` calls as `1`;
* drops positions that are invariant across the retained samples;
* recodes the **target** column to `3` (target reference) / `4` (target alternate)
  so that it gets its own colours in the legend;
* adds a left row annotation for the collection site and a top column annotation
  marking the target position in red;
* clusters rows with `hclust(dist(..., "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")`,
  keeping the columns in genomic order, and prints a check that the heatmap rows
  and the metadata rows are still aligned.

It is then applied to the 622I set (Gondar vs Eritrea) and to the 675V set
(Gambella vs Uganda vs South-East Asia), writing each heatmap to a PDF.

```{r,eval=FALSE}

make_flanking_heatmap <- function(
  bin_file,
  target,
  title,
  metadata,
  range
) {
  ## -------------------------
  ## Read & prepare matrix
  ## -------------------------
  mat <- bin_file

  mat[is.na(mat)] <- 0

  df <- as.matrix(mat)
  rownames(df) <- mat$pos
  df <- df[, -1]
  df <- t(df)

  full_data <- data.frame(sample = rownames(df), df, check.names = FALSE)
  full_data[full_data == 0.5] <- 1
  full_data[is.na(full_data)] <- 0
  full_data <- full_data[, colSums(full_data != 0) > 0]

  ## -------------------------
  ## Encode target locus
  ## -------------------------
  full_data[[as.character(target)]] <- ifelse(
    full_data[[as.character(target)]] == 1,
    4,
    ifelse(
      full_data[[as.character(target)]] == 0,
      3,
      full_data[[as.character(target)]]
    )
  )

  mat_final <- as.matrix(full_data[, -1])
  rownames(mat_final) <- full_data$sample

  ## -------------------------
  ## Row annotation (metadata)
  ## -------------------------
  metadata_2 <- metadata %>%
    filter(sample %in% rownames(mat_final)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample")
  metadata_2 <- metadata_2[rownames(mat_final), , drop = FALSE]
  site_colors <- c(
    "Ethiopia" = "#1b9e77", # teal-green
    "Uganda" = "#7570b3", # soft purple
    "south_east_asia" = "#66a61e", # olive green
    "Gondar" = "#e6ab02", # mustard yellow
    "Gambella" = "#d95f02", # orange-red (less harsh than pure red)
    "Eritria" = "#e7298a", # pink-magenta
    "unknown" = "#666666" # neutral gray (better than black)
  )

  ha_row <- rowAnnotation(
    site = metadata_2$site,
    col = list(site = site_colors)
  )

  ## -------------------------
  ## Column annotation (target)
  ## -------------------------
  ha_col <- columnAnnotation(
    Target = ifelse(colnames(mat_final) == target, "Target", ""),
    col = list(Target = c("Target" = "red")),
    show_annotation_name = FALSE,
    show_legend = FALSE
  )

  ## -------------------------
  ## Colors
  ## -------------------------
  col_fun <- colorRamp2(
    breaks = c(0, 1, 3, 4),
    colors = c(
      "#F2F2F2", # REF
      "#2C7FB8", # ALT
      "#f6ff00", # Target REF
      "#ff230a96" # Target ALT
    )
  )

  ## -------------------------
  ## Clustering
  ## -------------------------
  #rowcluster <- hclust(dist(mat_final), method = "ward.D2")
  rowcluster <- hclust(
    dist(mat_final, method = "euclidean"),
    method = "ward.D2"
  )
  # After reordering, verify alignment
  cat("Checking alignment:\n")
  cat("First 5 samples in heatmap:", head(rownames(mat_final)), "\n")
  cat("First 5 samples in metadata:", head(rownames(metadata_2)), "\n")
  cat(
    "Are they identical?",
    all(rownames(mat_final) == rownames(metadata_2)),
    "\n"
  )
  ## -------------------------
  ## Heatmap
  ## -------------------------
  Heatmap(
    mat_final,
    name = title,
    col = col_fun,
    cluster_rows = rowcluster,
    cluster_columns = FALSE,
    left_annotation = ha_row,
    top_annotation = ha_col,
    show_row_names = TRUE,
    show_column_names = FALSE,
    use_raster = FALSE,
    row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 8),
    column_title = paste0(
      title,
      " ",
      "Target: ",
      target,
      " ",
      "range= ",
      range
    ),
    heatmap_legend_param = list(
      title = "Genotype",
      at = c(0, 1, 3, 4),
      labels = c("REF", "ALT", "Target (REF)", "Target (ALT)")
    )
  )
}


metadata_1 <- gondar_sample_er_622I %>%

    )
```

### Repeat the flanking heatmaps using monoclonal samples only

The same windows and the same `make_flanking_heatmap()` call are repeated after
restricting both sample sets to monoclonal infections ($F_{WS} \ge 0.94$). This
removes the mixed-genotype samples, whose blended calls can create artificial
intermediate haplotypes and blur the cluster boundaries, so any shared haplotype
block seen here is more likely to be a real, single-strain haplotype.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
gondar_er_monoclonal <- gondar_sample_er_622I %>%
  filter(wgs_id %in% monoclonal$sample)

gambella_ug_monoclonal <- gambella_ug_se_675_samples %>%
  filter(sample %in% monoclonal$sample)

]
filtered_data_mono <- df_filtered_mono[

] # change this positions for start and end , the range size is 20000bp

df_filtered_675_mono <- all_mat_bin[,
  colnames(all_mat_bin) %in% c("pos", gambella_ug_monoclonal$sample)
]
# 675  position is 1724974
filtered_data_675_mono <- df_filtered_675_mono[
  df_filtered_675_mono$pos >= 1704974 & df_filtered_675_mono$pos <= 1744974,

ht2_mono <- make_flanking_heatmap(
```

## Assembly-based haplotypes with PathWeaver

### Collect the Gondar and Eritrean BAM files

The SNP-matrix approach above only uses called variants. To recover the actual
*sequence* haplotypes across the region, the reads themselves are re-assembled
per 200 bp window with PathWeaver. This chunk gathers the BAM files (and their
indexes) for the Gondar and Eritrean samples into a dedicated directory and
creates the `bed/` and `pathweaver_output/` folders used by the next steps. A
few samples fail to copy because of naming mismatches and were copied manually.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# total samples that are going to be extracted from gondar samples and ertria samples that are going to be extracted the region 
cd flanking_haplotype
ls  /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/*.bam  > all_samples.txt 


wc -l  /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/flanking_haplotype_updated/k13_gondar_eritrea/gondar_eritrea.txt

# used for copying gondar and ertria bam file to new directory , there are some samples which are not copying due to string mismatch i copied them manually
mkdir -p /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples
src="/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/"
dst="/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples"

while read sample; do
    cp "${src}/${sample}.bqsr.bam" "$dst/"
    cp "${src}/${sample}.bqsr.bam.bai" "$dst/"
done < /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/flanking_haplotype_updated/k13_gondar_eritrea/gondar_eritrea.txt

ls /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/*.bam |wc -l

# creating bed file for the k13 region
mkdir -p /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/bed

# creating output for the pathweaver

mkdir -p /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output
```

### Create the tiled BED file flanking the 622I variant

A table of drug-resistance associated loci is defined (AP2MU, AAT1, coronin,
ferredoxin, *k13*, *crt*, *mdr1*, *dhfr*, *dhps*, MCA2, KIC7, KIC5, KIC8, PX1)
and filtered to **k13** only (`Pf3D7_13_v3:1724817-1728000`). That region is then
cut into overlapping-free 200 bp windows, converted to 0-based BED coordinates,
and windows shorter than 50 bp (the trailing remainder) are dropped. Each window
becomes one PathWeaver "target", so the final heatmaps have one column per
200 bp window.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# I need to update the strand for each gene and also add additional targets
regions <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "AP2MU",
    "AAT1",
    "coronin",
    "ferredoxin",
    "k13",
    "crt",
    "mdr1",
    "dhfr",
    "dhps",
    "MCA2",
    "KIC7",
    "KIC5",
    "KIC8",
    "PX1"
  ),
  coord = c(
    "Pf3D7_12_v3:716700-720700",
    "Pf3D7_06_v3:1213100-1217350",
    "Pf3D7_12_v3:2091731-2094720",
    "Pf3D7_13_v3:748160-749415",
    "Pf3D7_13_v3:1724817-1728000",
    "Pf3D7_07_v3:403000-406000",
    "Pf3D7_05_v3:957500-962000",
    "Pf3D7_04_v3:746000-751000",
    "Pf3D7_08_v3:548000-552000",
    "Pf3D7_14_v3:1548072-1557053",
    "Pf3D7_08_v3:643066-645158",
    "Pf3D7_11_v3:1525654-1532527",
    "Pf3D7_10_v3:600950-608809",
    "Pf3D7_07_v3:889883-899213"
  ),
  strand = c(
    "+",
    "-",
    "+",
    "-",
    "-",
    "+",
    "+",
    "+",
    "+",
    "+",
    "-",
    "-",
    "-",
    "+"
  )
) %>%
  filter(name == "k13")

bed_windows <- regions %>%
  separate(coord, into = c("chr", "pos"), sep = ":") %>%
  separate(pos, into = c("region_start", "region_end"), sep = "-") %>%
  mutate(
    region_start = as.numeric(region_start),
    region_end = as.numeric(region_end)
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    windows = list(
      data.frame(
        start = seq(region_start, region_end, by = 200),
        end = pmin(seq(region_start, region_end, by = 200) + 199, region_end)
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(windows) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(start = start - 1) %>% # BED format
  select(chr, start, end, name, strand) %>%
  mutate(chr_pos = paste0(chr, "-", start, "-", end)) %>%
  mutate(length = end - start) %>%
  mutate(length = as.integer(length)) %>%
  filter(length > 50) %>%
  select(chr, start, end, chr_pos, length, strand)
write.table(
  bed_windows %>% select(chr, start, end, chr_pos, length, strand),
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/bed/kelch_region.bed",
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = FALSE
)
```

### Run the PathWeaver Nextflow pipeline over the BED windows

`pathweaver_extract_regions.nf` locally re-assembles the reads in each BED window
for every BAM, calls the haplotypes per window, and then clusters them across
samples into population haplotypes. `--qualCheck 20` drops low-quality bases
before assembly. The output lands in `pathweaver_output/`, whose
`allSelectedClustersInfo.tab.txt.gz` report drives the rainbow plot below.

```{bash,eval=FALSE}
conda activate nf-core
cd  /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples

# I put the output file in the genonotype_extraction folder
```

### Helper functions for the haplotype rainbow plots and clustering

Four reusable helpers are defined here:

* **`resort_prepped_samples_by_clustering()`** - keeps only targets that were
  successfully assembled in at least `target_sample_coverage_freq_cut_off` of
  samples, optionally reduces each sample/target to its major allele, builds a
  sample x haplotype presence/absence matrix, clusters it (Ward.D2 on Euclidean
  distance) and returns the data with the sample column re-levelled in
  dendrogram order so related samples sit next to each other in the plot.
* **`add_haplotype_rainbow_axis_theming()`** - restores the real target and
  sample labels on the numeric axes of the rainbow plot and rotates the x labels.
* **`createColorListFromDf()`** - generates a named colour vector per metadata
  column, expanding an RColorBrewer palette when there are more categories than
  the palette provides.
* **`matrix_to_tibble()`** - converts a square distance/similarity matrix into a
  long `sample1`/`sample2`/`value` tibble, optionally dropping the diagonal and
  the redundant lower triangle.
* **`single_linkage_clusters()`** - builds a graph linking every pair below a
  distance threshold and returns the connected components, i.e. single-linkage
  clusters of highly related samples.

```{r}
resort_prepped_samples_by_clustering <- function(
  prepped_allele_data,
  sampleCol = s_Sample,
  targetCol = p_name,
  popUIDCol = h_popUID,
  relAbundCol = c_AveragedFrac,
  target_sample_coverage_freq_cut_off = 0.80,
  by_major_allele = FALSE
) {
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(prepped_allele_data))

  # total distinct samples (used for coverage frequency)
  n_samples_total <- dplyr::n_distinct(dplyr::pull(
    prepped_allele_data,
    {{ sampleCol }}
  ))

  # targets with sufficient sample coverage
  targets_keep <- prepped_allele_data %>%
    ungroup() |>
    group_by({{ targetCol }}) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      sample_count = dplyr::n_distinct({{ sampleCol }})
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sample_freq = sample_count / n_samples_total) %>%
    dplyr::filter(sample_freq >= target_sample_coverage_freq_cut_off) %>%
    dplyr::pull({{ targetCol }}) |>
    unique()
  if (length(targets_keep) == 0) {
    stop("no targets above sample coverage cut off")
  }
  dat <- prepped_allele_data %>%
    filter({{ targetCol }} %in% targets_keep)

  # optionally keep only major allele per (sample, target)
  if (by_major_allele) {
    dat <- dat %>%
      dplyr::group_by({{ sampleCol }}, {{ targetCol }}) %>%
      dplyr::slice_max(
        order_by = {{ relAbundCol }},
        n = 1,
        with_ties = FALSE
      ) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()
  }

  # build sample x popUID presence/absence matrix
  dat_sp <- dat %>%
    mutate(new_identifier = paste0({{ targetCol }}, "-", {{ popUIDCol }})) |>
    ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select({{ sampleCol }}, new_identifier) %>%
    unique() |>
    dplyr::mutate(marker = 1L) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = new_identifier,
      values_from = marker,
      values_fill = 0L
    )

  # matrix for clustering
  dat_sp_mat <- as.matrix(dat_sp[, 2:ncol(dat_sp)])
  rownames(dat_sp_mat) <- dat_sp |>
    dplyr::pull({{ sampleCol }})
  dat_sp_mat_hc <- stats::hclust(stats::dist(dat_sp_mat), method = "ward.D2")
  sample_levels <- rownames(dat_sp_mat)[dat_sp_mat_hc$order]

  # add any samples that were filtered off to the end
  any_missing_samples <- prepped_allele_data %>%
    filter(!({{ sampleCol }} %in% sample_levels)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    dplyr::pull({{ sampleCol }})

  sample_levels <- c(
    as.character(sample_levels),
    as.character(any_missing_samples)
  )

  prepped_allele_data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      {{ sampleCol }} := factor({{ sampleCol }}, levels = sample_levels)
    )
}


add_haplotype_rainbow_axis_theming <- function(
  rainbow_plot,
  prepped_allele_data,
  sampleCol = s_Sample,
  targetCol = p_name
) {
  target_levels <- levels(prepped_allele_data |> pull({{ targetCol }}))
  sample_levels <- levels(prepped_allele_data |> pull({{ sampleCol }}))
  return(
    rainbow_plot +
      scale_x_continuous(
        labels = target_levels,
        breaks = 1:n_distinct(target_levels),
        expand = c(0, 0)
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(
        labels = sample_levels,
        breaks = 1:n_distinct(sample_levels),
        expand = c(0, 0)
      ) +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(family = "mono"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(family = "mono", angle = -90, hjust = 0)
      )
  )
}

createColorListFromDf <- function(df, palette = "Accent") {
  # Load required package
  library(RColorBrewer)

  color_lists <- list()

  for (col_name in colnames(df)) {
    # Get unique categories
    categories <- unique(as.character(df[[col_name]]))

    # Generate colors
    n_colors <- length(categories)

    if (n_colors <= 8) {
      colors <- brewer.pal(max(3, n_colors), palette)[1:n_colors]
    } else {
      colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, palette))(n_colors)
    }

    # Create mapping
    color_map <- setNames(colors, categories)

    # Map colors to rows
    color_lists[[col_name]] <- color_map[as.character(df[[col_name]])]
  }

  return(color_lists)
}


matrix_to_tibble <- function(
  mat,
  dist_col_name = "distance",
  upper_tri_only = FALSE,
  include_diagonal = FALSE
) {
  # Validate input
  if (!is.matrix(mat)) {
    mat <- as.matrix(mat)
  }
  if (is.null(rownames(mat)) || is.null(colnames(mat))) {
    stop("Matrix must have both row names and column names.")
  }

  # Convert to long format tibble
  result <- mat |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    rownames_to_column(var = "sample1") |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -sample1,
      names_to = "sample2",
      values_to = dist_col_name
    ) |>
    as_tibble()

  # Optionally remove diagonal (self-comparisons)
  if (!include_diagonal) {
    result <- result |> filter(sample1 != sample2)
  }

  # Optionally keep only upper triangle
  if (upper_tri_only) {
    # Keep pairs where sample1 appears before sample2 in the row name order
    sample_levels <- rownames(mat)
    result <- result |>
      filter(
        match(sample1, sample_levels) < match(sample2, sample_levels)
      )
  }

  return(result)
}


single_linkage_clusters <- function(
  df,
  distance_col,
  threshold,
  sample_col = sample,
  other_sample_col = other_sample
) {
  edges <- df %>%
    filter({{ distance_col }} <= threshold) %>%
    transmute(
      from = as.character({{ sample_col }}),
      to = as.character({{ other_sample_col }})
    )

  verts <- tibble(
    name = unique(c(
      as.character(df |> pull({{ sample_col }})),
      as.character(df |> pull({{ other_sample_col }}))
    ))
  )

  g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE, vertices = verts)

  comps <- components(g)$membership

  tibble(
    sample = names(comps),
    cluster = as.integer(comps)
  ) %>%
    arrange(cluster, sample)
}
```

### Haplotype rainbow plot of the *k13* region, annotated by site and 622I genotype

This is the main assembly-based figure. The PathWeaver
`allSelectedClustersInfo` report is read and the sample names are normalised
(sequencing suffixes such as `_S12`, `_libLAN*` and the `NG-A4488_` prefix are
stripped, `-D0` is rewritten to `_D0`) so that they match the metadata tables.

Samples and targets are then filtered:

* only monoclonal samples ($F_{WS} > 0.95$), with `WG24GMHC015` excluded;
* only samples with at least 15 assembled targets;
* only targets recovered in more than 40% of samples - a deliberately relaxed
  cut-off, because many 200 bp windows do not assemble in every sample.

`prepForRainbow()` converts the filtered table to the rainbow layout, samples are
re-ordered by haplotype-sharing clustering, and each haplotype gets its own
colour. Two annotation bars are then drawn to the left of the plot with
`geom_rect()` on a new fill scale: **Site** and the **K13 622I genotype**
(samples absent from the 622I table are set to `0/0`, i.e. wild type). The
figure is written to both PNG and PDF at 20x20 inches.

## Pairwise haplotype sharing (Jaccard)

### Compute the pairwise Jaccard matrix with elucidator

Already run once - re-running is only needed if the input table changes, and
`--overWriteDir` should be used with care because it deletes the existing output
directory. `doPairwiseComparisonOnHapsSharing` compares every pair of samples
and, among the targets both samples share, computes the Jaccard index of their
haplotypes (shared haplotypes / total haplotypes). `--writeOutDistMatrices`
emits the square matrices consumed by the next chunk.

```{bash,eval=F}
cd /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/
ls /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/

docker run -it   -v /mnt/storage13/ahri:/data   nickjhathaway/elucidator:develop elucidator doPairwiseComparisonOnHapsSharing  --tableFnp /data/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/updated_allSelectedClustersInfo_monos_k13_region_filt.tsv  --sampleCol s_Sample --targetNameCol p_name --popIDCol h_Consensus --relAbundCol c_ReadCnt --dout /data/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/pairwise_comps_updated_allSelectedClustersInfo_mono_k13_622 --writeOutDistMatrices --overWriteDir
```



### Read the Jaccard matrix and attach the sample metadata

`sampleNames.tab.txt` gives the row/column order of the matrix, which is bound to
`jacardByHapsTarShared.tab.txt.gz` to build a named square matrix. A
blue-white-red colour ramp is defined over the 0-1 Jaccard range, and the
$F_{WS} > 0.95$ metadata (country, site) is re-ordered with `match()` so it lines
up row-for-row with the matrix.

```{r}

  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/supplementary_Data/supp_fws_up.tsv",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  filter(fws > 0.95) %>%
  select(sample_id, Country, fws, Site)

  col_names = "sample"
)

jacardByHapsTarShared <- bind_cols(
  sample_names,
  readr::read_tsv(
    "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/pairwise_comps_updated_allSelectedClustersInfo_mono_k13_622/jacardByHapsTarShared.tab.txt.gz",
    col_names = sample_names$sample
  )
)


jacardByHapsTarShared_mat <- as.matrix(jacardByHapsTarShared[,
  2:ncol(jacardByHapsTarShared)
])
rownames(jacardByHapsTarShared_mat) <- jacardByHapsTarShared$sample

library(circlize)
cols <- circlize::colorRamp2(c(0, 0.5, 1), c("#2b83ba", "#f7f7f7", "#d7191c"))


sample_meta_for_jaccard <- suppleme_fws[
  match(rownames(jacardByHapsTarShared_mat), suppleme_fws$sample_id),
]
```

```{r}
)] <- "0/0"

  sample_meta_for_jaccard_df
)

  gp = gpar(color = "black")
```

### Single-linkage clustering and a colour-consistent Jaccard heatmap

The same Jaccard matrix is reworked with tighter control over the colours. The
matrix is flattened to a long tibble (upper triangle only), converted to a
distance (`1 - jaccard`) and passed to `single_linkage_clusters()` with a
threshold of 0.05 - so any two samples sharing at least 95% of their haplotypes
are joined, and the connected components become clonal-lineage clusters.

`create_consistent_colors()` then fixes the palette per annotation (hard-coded
country and genotype colours, Brewer ramps for site and cluster) and the *same*
list is reused for the row annotation, the column annotation and the manually
built legends. This guarantees that a given country/genotype is the same colour
everywhere, which was not the case when the colours were regenerated separately.
Legends are drawn manually with `Legend()`/`packLegend()` and the figure is saved
as PNG and PDF.

```{r}
library(igraph)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. PREPARE DATA
# ==============================================================================

# Your existing data preparation
jacardByHapsTarShared_mat_1unique_chr11 <- jacardByHapsTarShared_mat

# Get sample metadata

sample_meta_df$genotype <- trimws(sample_meta_df$genotype)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. CREATE CONSISTENT COLOR PALETTES (FIXED)
# ==============================================================================

# Function to create consistent color mapping
create_consistent_colors <- function(df) {
  color_list <- list()
  
  # Country colors
  if ("Country" %in% colnames(df)) {
    countries <- sort(unique(na.omit(df$Country)))
    country_palette <- c(
      "Ethiopia" = "#2E86AB", 
      
      "Eritrea" = "#F18F01",
      "Somalia" = "#4DAF4A"
    )
    # Only keep countries that exist in data
    color_list$Country <- country_palette[names(country_palette) %in% countries]
    # Add any missing countries with new colors
    missing_countries <- setdiff(countries, names(color_list$Country))
    if (length(missing_countries) > 0) {
      new_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set1"))(length(missing_countries))
      names(new_colors) <- missing_countries
      color_list$Country <- c(color_list$Country, new_colors)
    }
  }
  
  # Site colors
  if ("Site" %in% colnames(df)) {
    sites <- sort(unique(na.omit(df$Site)))
    site_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))(length(sites))
    names(site_colors) <- sites
    color_list$Site <- site_colors
  }
  
  # Genotype colors
  if ("genotype" %in% colnames(df)) {
    genotypes <- sort(unique(na.omit(df$genotype)))
    # Define standard genotype colors
    genotype_palette <- c(
      "0/0" = "#E41A1C",
      "0/1" = "#377EB8",
      "1/1" = "#4DAF4A",
      "./." = "#984EA3",
      "0|0" = "#E41A1C",
      "0|1" = "#377EB8",
      "1|1" = "#4DAF4A"
    )
    # Only keep genotypes that exist
    color_list$genotype <- genotype_palette[names(genotype_palette) %in% genotypes]
    # Add any missing genotypes
    missing_genotypes <- setdiff(genotypes, names(color_list$genotype))
    if (length(missing_genotypes) > 0) {
      new_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set3"))(length(missing_genotypes))
      names(new_colors) <- missing_genotypes
      color_list$genotype <- c(color_list$genotype, new_colors)
    }
  }
  
  # Cluster colors
  if ("cluster" %in% colnames(df)) {
    clusters <- sort(unique(na.omit(df$cluster)))
    cluster_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))(length(clusters))
    names(cluster_colors) <- clusters
    color_list$cluster <- cluster_colors
  }
  
  return(color_list)
}

# Create consistent color mapping
annotation_colors <- create_consistent_colors(sample_meta_df)

# Print color mapping for verification
cat("\nColor mapping:\n")
print(annotation_colors)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. CREATE ANNOTATIONS WITH CONSISTENT COLORS
# ==============================================================================

# Row annotation - using the SAME color mapping
sample_meta_df_anno <- rowAnnotation(
  df = sample_meta_df,
  col = annotation_colors,  # Use the same color mapping
  gp = gpar(color = "black"),

)

# Column annotation - using the SAME color mapping
sample_meta_df_top_anno <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  df = sample_meta_df,
  col = annotation_colors,  # Use the same color mapping
  gp = gpar(color = "black"),
  show_annotation_name = TRUE,
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12, fontface = "italic"),
  show_legend = FALSE
)

# ==============================================================================
# 5. CREATE HEATMAP
# ==============================================================================

# Define color palette for Jaccard values
col_jaccard <- colorRamp2(
  c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1),
  c("#FFFFFF", "#FDE0DD", "#FBB4B9", "#F768A1", "#C51B8A", "#7A0177")
)

# Create heatmap
jacardByHapsTarShared_mat_1unique_chr11_hp <- ComplexHeatmap::Heatmap(
  jacardByHapsTarShared_mat_1unique_chr11,
  col = col_jaccard,
  name = "Jaccard",
  row_dend_width = unit(5, "cm"),

  left_annotation = sample_meta_df_anno,
  top_annotation = sample_meta_df_top_anno,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = TRUE,
  # clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  # clustering_distance_columns = "euclidean",
  # clustering_method_rows = "ward.D2",
  # clustering_method_columns = "ward.D2",
  show_row_names = TRUE,
  show_column_names = FALSE,
  show_heatmap_legend = FALSE
)

# ==============================================================================
# 6. CREATE LEGENDS
# ==============================================================================

# Function to create legends from color mapping
create_legends <- function(color_list) {
  legends <- list()
  
  for (name in names(color_list)) {
    colors <- color_list[[name]]
    if (length(colors) > 0) {
      legends[[name]] <- Legend(
        title = name,
        at = names(colors),
        legend_gp = gpar(fill = colors),
        title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
        labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
        grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
        grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
      )
    }
  }
  
  return(legends)
}

# Create legends for each annotation
annotation_legends <- create_legends(annotation_colors)

# Add Jaccard legend
jaccard_legend <- Legend(
  col_fun = col_jaccard,
  title = "Jaccard",
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
  grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
)

# Combine all legends
all_legends <- c(annotation_legends, list(jaccard_legend))

# Pack legends
pack_master <- do.call(
  packLegend,
  c(
    all_legends,
    list(direction = "vertical", gap = unit(8, "mm"))
  )
)

# ==============================================================================
# 7. SAVE PLOT
# ==============================================================================

# Create the plot

png(
  "ouput/figure/jacard_flanking_haplotype_622_filtered.png",
  width = 20,
  height = 20,
  units = "in",

)

draw(jacardByHapsTarShared_mat_1unique_chr11_hp,
annotation_legend_list = pack_master,

dev.off()

)

draw(jacardByHapsTarShared_mat_1unique_chr11_hp,
```

## Comparing haplotype sharing with genome-wide relatedness

### Build a split heatmap: hmmIBD below the diagonal, Jaccard above it

This chunk asks whether samples that share *k13* flanking haplotypes are also
related genome-wide. The `hmmIBD` output (`fract_sites_IBD` per pair) is read and
restricted to the pairs that also have a Jaccard value, using an order-independent
`pair_id` built with `pmin()`/`pmax()`. Self-comparisons are added with a value of
1 so the diagonal is complete.

Two symmetric matrices are filled over the same sample set (monoclonal,
$F_{WS} > 0.95$), and the samples are ordered by country, then site, then 622I
genotype rather than by clustering, so the geographic blocks are directly
comparable between the two halves. Genotype strings are cleaned first (leftover
`b'...'` byte encoding, quotes, whitespace, `|` to `/`) because otherwise the
annotation colours silently fail to match.

The heatmap is drawn with `rect_gp = gpar(type = "none")` and a custom
`layer_fun`, which paints each cell manually: the **lower triangle** uses the IBD
colour ramp (binned at 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8), the **upper triangle** uses the Jaccard
ramp, and the diagonal is black. All legends are packed manually and the figure
is written to PDF and PNG.

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD AND PREPARE DATA
# ==============================================================================

# Load your data
all_hmmibd_fract <- read.table(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/hmmIBD/all_samples/hmmIBD_sample_maf0.01.out.hmm_fract.txt",
  header = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  select(sample1, sample2, fract_sites_IBD) %>%
  mutate(
    pair_id = paste(
      pmin(sample1, sample2),
      pmax(sample1, sample2),
      sep = "_"
    )
  )

# Your Jaccard data
jacard2 <- jacardByHapsTarShared_mat_1unique_chr11_tib %>%
  mutate(
    pair_id = paste(
      pmin(sample1, sample2),
      pmax(sample1, sample2),
      sep = "_"
    )
  )

# Filter IBD to only pairs present in Jaccard
high_ibd <- all_hmmibd_fract %>%
  filter(pair_id %in% jacard2$pair_id)

# FWS filter - samples with FWS > 0.95
fws_filtered <- suppleme_fws %>%
  filter(fws > 0.95) %>%
  select(sample_id, Country, fws, Site)
# Create merged plot dataframe
plot_df <- merge(
  high_ibd,
  jacard2,
  by = "pair_id"
) %>%
  select(sample1.x, sample2.x, fract_sites_IBD, jaccard) %>%
  dplyr::rename(sample1 = sample1.x, sample2 = sample2.x)

unique1_sample <- unique(plot_df$sample1)

similar_samples <- data.frame(
  sample1 = unique1_sample,
  sample2 = unique1_sample,
  fract_sites_IBD = 1,
  jaccard = 1
)

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(similar_samples)
# ==============================================================================
# 2. BUILD MATRICES FOR HEATMAP
# ==============================================================================

# Get unique samples from both matrices (only those with FWS > 0.95)
# ==============================================================================
# 2. BUILD MATRICES FOR HEATMAP
# ==============================================================================

# Get unique samples from both matrices (only those with FWS > 0.95)
fws_samples <- fws_filtered$sample_id
all_samples <- unique(c(plot_df$sample1, plot_df$sample2))
samples_to_keep <- intersect(all_samples, fws_samples)

# Create empty matrices
n_samples <- length(samples_to_keep)
mat_ibd <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_samples, ncol = n_samples)
mat_jaccard <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_samples, ncol = n_samples)
rownames(mat_ibd) <- colnames(mat_ibd) <- samples_to_keep
rownames(mat_jaccard) <- colnames(mat_jaccard) <- samples_to_keep

# Fill matrices
for (i in seq_len(nrow(plot_df))) {
  s1 <- plot_df$sample1[i]
  s2 <- plot_df$sample2[i]

  if (s1 %in% samples_to_keep && s2 %in% samples_to_keep) {
    mat_ibd[s1, s2] <- mat_ibd[s2, s1] <- plot_df$fract_sites_IBD[i]
    mat_jaccard[s1, s2] <- mat_jaccard[s2, s1] <- plot_df$jaccard[i]
  }
}

# Set diagonals
diag(mat_ibd) <- 1
diag(mat_jaccard) <- 1

# ==============================================================================
# 3. METADATA AND ORDERING (FIXED GENOTYPE ISSUE)
# ==============================================================================

# Create metadata for the samples
sample_meta <- fws_filtered %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% samples_to_keep) %>%
  select(sample_id, Country, Site) %>%
  left_join(
    k13_622I %>% select(sample, genotype),
    by = c("sample_id" = "sample")
  )

# FIX 1: Clean genotype column - remove any byte encoding and whitespace
sample_meta$genotype <- as.character(sample_meta$genotype) # Convert to character
sample_meta$genotype <- gsub("b'|'", "", sample_meta$genotype) # Remove b' and '
sample_meta$genotype <- trimws(sample_meta$genotype) # Remove whitespace

# FIX 2: Replace NAs with "0/0"
sample_meta$genotype[is.na(sample_meta$genotype)] <- "0/0"

# FIX 3: Clean any other unexpected characters
sample_meta$genotype <- gsub('[""]', "", sample_meta$genotype) # Remove quotes

# FIX 4: Standardize genotype notation (optional - if you have different formats)
# Convert "1/1" and "1|1" to same format if needed
sample_meta$genotype <- gsub("\\|", "/", sample_meta$genotype) # Convert | to /

# Check unique genotype values after cleaning
cat("Unique genotype values after cleaning:\n")
print(unique(sample_meta$genotype))

# Order samples by Country, Site, genotype
ordering_df <- sample_meta %>%
  arrange(Country, Site, genotype, sample_id)

order_idx <- match(ordering_df$sample_id, rownames(mat_ibd))

# Reorder matrices
mat_ibd <- mat_ibd[order_idx, order_idx, drop = FALSE]
mat_jaccard <- mat_jaccard[order_idx, order_idx, drop = FALSE]

# ==============================================================================
# 4. CREATE COLOR PALETTES (FIXED)
# ==============================================================================

# Prepare annotations with consistent colors
country_colors <- c("Ethiopia" = "#2E86AB",  "Eritrea" = "#F18F01")

# Site colors
unique_sites <- unique(ordering_df$Site)
site_palette <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))(length(unique_sites))
site_colors <- setNames(site_palette, unique_sites)

# FIX 5: Genotype colors - ensure all genotype values are properly named
unique_genotypes <- unique(ordering_df$genotype)
# Create a clean genotype color palette
genotype_palette <- c(
  "0/0" = "#E41A1C", # Red for reference
  "0/1" = "#377EB8", # Blue for heterozygous
  "b'1/1'" = "#4DAF4A", # Green for homozygous alternate
  "./." = "#984EA3", # Purple for missing
  "NA" = "#FF7F00" # Orange for NA
)

# Only keep colors for genotypes that actually exist in your data
existing_genotypes <- intersect(names(genotype_palette), unique_genotypes)
genotype_colors <- genotype_palette[existing_genotypes]

# If there are genotypes not in the palette, add them with new colors
new_genotypes <- setdiff(unique_genotypes, names(genotype_palette))
if (length(new_genotypes) > 0) {
  new_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set3"))(length(new_genotypes))
  names(new_colors) <- new_genotypes
  genotype_colors <- c(genotype_colors, new_colors)
}

cat("\nGenotype color mapping:\n")
print(genotype_colors)

# ==============================================================================
# 5. VERIFY ANNOTATION COLOR MAPPING
# ==============================================================================

# Check that all values in genotype column have colors defined
genotype_values <- unique(ordering_df$genotype)
missing_colors <- setdiff(genotype_values, names(genotype_colors))

if (length(missing_colors) > 0) {
  cat(
    "Warning: Missing colors for genotypes:",
    paste(missing_colors, collapse = ", "),
    "\n"
  )
  # Add colors for missing genotypes
  additional_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set3"))(length(
    missing_colors
  ))
  names(additional_colors) <- missing_colors
  genotype_colors <- c(genotype_colors, additional_colors)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 6. CREATE ANNOTATIONS (FIXED)
# ==============================================================================

# Create annotation color list
annotation_colors <- list(
  Country = country_colors,
  Site = site_colors,
  genotype = genotype_colors
)

# Row annotation
row_ha <- rowAnnotation(
  Country = ordering_df$Country,
  Site = ordering_df$Site,
  genotype = ordering_df$genotype,
  col = annotation_colors,
  show_annotation_name = TRUE,
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "italic"),
  show_legend = FALSE
)

# Column annotation
col_ha <- HeatmapAnnotation(
  Country = ordering_df$Country,
  Site = ordering_df$Site,
  genotype = ordering_df$genotype,
  col = annotation_colors,
  show_annotation_name = TRUE,
  annotation_name_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "italic"),
  show_legend = FALSE
)

# ==============================================================================
# 7. CREATE HEATMAP
# ==============================================================================

# Color palettes for heatmap
col_ibd <- colorRamp2(
    c(0, 0.2, 0.2+1e-8, 0.5, 0.5+1e-8, 0.8, 0.8+1e-8, 1),
    c("#FFFFFF", "#FFFFFF",
      "#ddd057", "#ddd057",
      "#6D819E", "#6D819E",
      "#102A43", "#102A43")
)

col_jaccard <- colorRamp2(
  c(0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1),
  c("#FFFFFF", "#FDE0DD", "#FBB4B9", "#F768A1", "#C51B8A", "#7A0177")
)

# Main heatmap with custom layer function
ht <- Heatmap(
  mat_ibd,
  name = "IBD / Jaccard",
  col = col_ibd,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  left_annotation = row_ha,
  top_annotation = col_ha,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
  show_heatmap_legend = FALSE,
  border = TRUE,
  rect_gp = gpar(type = "none"),
  use_raster = TRUE,
  raster_quality = 5,
  layer_fun = function(j, i, x, y, w, h, fill) {
    # Lower triangle: IBD values
    sel_low <- i > j
    if (any(sel_low)) {
      vals_ibd <- mat_ibd[cbind(i[sel_low], j[sel_low])]
      grid.rect(
        x[sel_low],
        y[sel_low],
        w[sel_low],
        h[sel_low],
        gp = gpar(fill = col_ibd(vals_ibd), col = NA)
      )
    }

    # Upper triangle: Jaccard values
    sel_up <- i < j
    if (any(sel_up)) {
      vals_jaccard <- mat_jaccard[cbind(i[sel_up], j[sel_up])]
      grid.rect(
        x[sel_up],
        y[sel_up],
        w[sel_up],
        h[sel_up],
        gp = gpar(fill = col_jaccard(vals_jaccard), col = NA)
      )
    }

    # Diagonal: grey
    sel_diag <- i == j
    if (any(sel_diag)) {
      grid.rect(
        x[sel_diag],
        y[sel_diag],
        w[sel_diag],
        h[sel_diag],
        gp = gpar(fill = "black", col = NA)
      )
    }
  }
)

# ==============================================================================
# 8. LEGENDS
# ==============================================================================

lgd_ibd <- Legend(
  col_fun = col_ibd,
  title = "IBD (fraction)",
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
  grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
)

lgd_jaccard <- Legend(
  col_fun = col_jaccard,
  title = "Jaccard",
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
  grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
)

lgd_country <- Legend(
  title = "Country",
  at = names(country_colors),
  legend_gp = gpar(fill = country_colors),
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
  grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
)

lgd_site <- Legend(
  title = "Site",
  at = names(site_colors),
  legend_gp = gpar(fill = site_colors),
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
  grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
)

lgd_genotype <- Legend(
  title = "Genotype",
  at = names(genotype_colors),
  legend_gp = gpar(fill = genotype_colors),
  title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"),
  labels_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
  grid_height = unit(6, "mm"),
  grid_width = unit(6, "mm")
)

# Pack legends
pack_master <- packLegend(
  lgd_country,
  lgd_site,
  lgd_genotype,
  lgd_ibd,
  lgd_jaccard,
  direction = "vertical",
  gap = unit(8, "mm")
)

pdf(
  "ouput/figure/jacard_hmmIBD_flanking_haplotype_622_filt_corrected.pdf",
  width = 20,
  height = 20,
  bg = "white"
)

draw(
    ht,
      annotation_legend_list = pack_master,
        heatmap_legend_side = "right",
          annotation_legend_side = "right",
            padding = unit(c(5, 5, 5, 5), "mm")
            )


dev.off()
# ==============================================================================
# 9. SAVE PLOT
# ==============================================================================

out_dir <- "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/whole_genome_scripts/flanking_haplotype/flanking_haplotype_k13/ouput/figure"
# dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Create the plot
png(
  "ouput/figure/jacard_hmmIBD_flanking_haplotype_622_filt_corrected.png",
  width = 20,
  height = 20,
  units = "in",
  res = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
draw(
  ht,
   annotation_legend_list = pack_master,
```

## Genetic diversity across the *k13* windows

### Prepare the PathWeaver metadata file

To let PathWeaver compute population-genetic statistics per group, a metadata
file is assembled. The *k13* 622 metadata is restricted to Ethiopia and Eritrea
and a `k13_622_genotype` column is derived (`mutant` when the mutation string
contains `R622I`, otherwise `wildtype`). The sample identifiers in the PathWeaver
`allBasicInfo` report are normalised in the same way as before and joined to the
metadata, so that the file uses exactly the identifiers PathWeaver expects.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
kelch_metadata <- read.csv("/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/logestic_regression/hrp_status/kelch_622_metadata.csv",header=T)%>%
  filter(Country %in% c("Ethiopia","Eritrea"))%>%
  mutate(k13_622_genotype = ifelse(grepl("R622I", mutation_test), "mutant" , "wildtype"))%>%
  dplyr::select(Sample,Country,Site,k13_622_genotype,fws)
print(length(unique(kelch_metadata$sample)))
# i got the pathweaver output to extract the samples that i need to use for the metadata information 
allbasicinfo <- readr::read_tsv("/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/PathWeaverResults/reports/populationClustering/reports/allBasicInfo.tab.txt.gz",col_names = T)%>%
  select(sample)%>%
  distinct()%>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample))  %>% 
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>% 
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>% 
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample))
print(length(unique(allbasicinfo$Sample)))
kelch_metadata_merged <- allbasicinfo %>%
  left_join(kelch_metadata, by = c("Sample" = "Sample"))%>%
  dplyr::select(sample,Country,Site,k13_622_genotype,fws)%>%
  dplyr::rename(Sample = sample)
print(length(unique(kelch_metadata_merged$Sample)))

write_tsv(kelch_metadata_merged ,"/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/kelch_622_metadata.tsv")
```
### Re-run PathWeaver with metadata and variant calling for population statistics

The same pipeline is run again, this time with `--meta_fnp` pointing at the
metadata file, `--meta_fields_to_calc_pop_diffs Country,Site,K13_622_genotype`
to request between-group differentiation statistics, and `--do_variant_calling`
to produce the diversity reports. `--pw_pop_clustering_ncpus 1` is required
because the clustering step core-dumped with multiple threads. Note that a
number of samples are not present in the metadata file and are therefore skipped.

```{bash,eval=FALSE}
conda activate nf-core
cd  /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples

mkdir -p /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/popstat 

# there was a core dumpe so i decrease the thread to 1 and it works but there are a lot of samples which are not found in the metadata 
nextflow run /mnt/storage13/ahri/hrp2_analysis/elucidatornf/pathweaver_extract_regions.nf --bams_dir ./ --pw_bed_fnp /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/bed/kelch_region.bed   --genome_fnp /mnt/storage13/ahri/hrp2_analysis/pf_genomes/genomes/Pf3D7.fasta --outdir /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/popstat/ --bams_file_ending ".bam" --pw_extract_region_assemblies_extra_args="--qualCheck 20" -profile apptainer --meta_fnp /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/kelch_622_metadata.tsv  --pw_pop_clustering_ncpus 1 --meta_fields_to_calc_pop_diffs Country,Site,K13_622_genotype  --do_variant_calling

ls /mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/popstat/
```

### Expected heterozygosity, coverage and haplotype counts per target

`allDiversityMeasures.tsv.gz` reports one row per 200 bp target. Three stacked
panels are built with **patchwork**:

* **He** - expected heterozygosity, i.e. how diverse each window is. Windows
  around a recently selected variant are expected to show reduced diversity.
* **Sample count** - how many samples assembled that window, which shows whether a
  low He is real or simply the result of poor coverage.
* **Total haplotypes** - the number of distinct sequence haplotypes per window.

The x-axis labels are removed from the top two panels because all three share the
same target ordering. The combined figure is saved at 8 x 10 inches, 300 dpi.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
  all_diversity_measures <- readr::read_tsv("/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/pfalciparum_09_24_v2/cram/gondar_ertria_samples/pathweaver_output/popstat/PathWeaverResults/variantCalls/reports/popGenetics/allDiversityMeasures.tsv.gz")

library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
df <- all_diversity_measures
# He
p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(target, he)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Expected heterozygosity", x = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

# Sample count
p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(target, sampleCount)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Sample count", x = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

# Total haplotypes
p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(target, totalHaplotypes)) +
  geom_col(fill = "tomato") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Total haplotypes", x = "Target") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

p1 / p2 / p3
combined_plot <- p1 / p2 / p3

ggsave(
  filename = "ouput/figure/k13_hetrozygosity_region.png",
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 8,      # inches
  height = 10,    # inches
  dpi = 300       # publication quality
)
```
